A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, experiments, tables, figures, and equations can be matched despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original relation-extraction experiments, including FS-TACRED and FS-FewRel results, a parametric-knowledge probe, and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports component runtimes and statistical significance comparisons.

M1.justification: The binary ICL procedure, entity-type filtering, semantic-rule retrieval, clustering, hybrid selection, and optional summarization remain the same. Prompt wording and illustrative entity-label corrections do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UMBC retrieval pool, FS-TACRED, and six-relation FS-FewRel subset. Both also evaluate FS-NYT29 in the appendix parametric-knowledge probe, despite excluding it from the main experiments.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains MNAV, OdinSynth, CKPT, SoftRules, and Anchor + generated rules with unchanged scores; only row ordering changes. The LLM-generation, paraphrasing, and SBERT comparisons are also retained. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds runtime evaluation with component timings and per-episode accounting for the hybrid and LLM-generated approaches. The accuracy experiments retain their episode sets, shot counts, four LLM configurations, metrics, threshold, and decoding settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds a computational-efficiency analysis and corrects subject/object annotations in the clustered-retrieval examples of v1 Table 6, now Table 3. The clustering, summarization, diversity, NER-filtering, and binary-versus-multiclass analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: V1 reports means and standard deviations without significance tests. V2 adds one-sided paired bootstrap tests with replacement on F1 across the main and extended comparisons, with p < 0.05 and p < 0.01 markers in Tables 1 and 5–9. This introduces inferential testing across the central results; additional runs or changed seeds are not documented.

E6.justification: Matched accuracy scores and standard deviations are unchanged, including Table 1's Qwen3-4B hybrid 1+9 F1 of 27.6 ± 1.20. V2 adds significance outcomes and runtime results, including 6.9 seconds for retrieval/clustering, 8.95 seconds for generation, and 0.049 seconds for selection. Qualitative example roles are also corrected.

T1.justification: The episodic task formulation and rule for determining the number of clusters remain mathematically equivalent. Changes from N/n to n/m are notation edits. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its SOTA contribution from FSRE generally to FS-TACRED and identifies semantic representations of lexico-syntactic rules as the key retrieval novelty. The principal hybrid-selection, transfer, and similarity/diversity claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 qualifies the three-of-four superiority observation as applying to hybrid systems, and adds context about prior methods using smaller fine-tuned models. Section 7 introduces a negligible-runtime-overhead interpretation, although its 0.5% claim is not reconciled with the listed retrieval cost. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that code and data are available through a repository and supplies component timing information. Appendix A retains the same threshold, FAISS reuse description, decoding parameters, and output-token limit. Repository availability is stated in the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of FSRE, ICL retrieval, diversity, and LLM-based data generation, including GPT-RE and C-ICL. A new similarity-and-diversity subsection accompanies a narrower novelty claim: syntactic-semantic retrieval for FSRE replaces the broader claim of first improving ICL example selection through similarity and diversity.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits the title, abstract, body, and prompt templates; regularizes 1-shot and entity terminology; and adds acknowledgements. Explanations are refined locally, while the overall section sequence and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with stacked branches and fewer displayed examples. Eight retained prompt tables become Figures 2–9, with some appendix rearrangement. Result tables retain their structure while gaining significance symbols and explanatory captions.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision and usability through narrower novelty claims, better research positioning, corrected example roles, and code/data access information. Significance reporting adds context to unchanged accuracy results. The gain is limited by underspecified bootstrap details and the new 0.5% runtime claim, whose accounting does not clearly include the reported 6.9-second retrieval cost.
